Nirmal Pol

PhD Candidate, Biomedical Engineering

I’m a PhD candidate in the MEDCVR Lab at the University of Toronto, supervised by Prof. Lueder A. Kahrs.

My research focuses on perception and control for surgical robotics. I use optical coherence tomography (OCT), an imaging technique that captures micron-scale subsurface detail, to estimate surgical tool motion and guide precise robotic manipulation.

Publications

SuMI: Zero-Shot Policy Transfer between Different Robots with Wristed Instruments for Minimally Invasive Surgery

Nirmal Pol*, Radian Gondokaryono*, Puspita Triana Dewi, Fata A. Niazi, Jones Law, Kashfia Mahmood, Lueder A. Kahrs
Manuscript under review (2026)

Transfers a policy learned on a Franka arm with wristed surgical instruments to the da Vinci Research Kit without retraining, achieving 17/20 successful angled peg-transfer trials.

Paper Code Video Website

OCT Imaging for Pose Estimation and Feedback Control of an Articulated Magnetic Surgical Tool

Erik Fredin*, Nirmal Pol*, Anton Zaliznyi, Dmytro Fishman, Eric Diller, Lueder A. Kahrs
Robotics and Automation Letters (RAL) (2025)

8 DoF pose estimation of magnetically actuated micro-robotic gripper for neurosurgical applications using OCT imaging for closed-loop control.

Paper Code Video Website

Estimating the Joint Angles of an Articulated Microrobotic Instrument using Optical Coherence Tomography

Erik Fredin*, Nirmal Pol*, Anton Zaliznyi*, Eric Diller, Lueder A. Kahrs
International Symposium on Medical Robotics (ISMR) (2024)

Performed 3D template matching on volumetric OCT images to detect spherical markers and estimate micro-robot joint angles.

Paper Video

Pose Measurement of the EndoWrist Round Tip Scissor Instrument with Optical Coherence Tomography

Sandra Schoene, Nirmal Pol, Lueder A. Kahrs
Current Directions in Biomedical Engineering, vol 9 (2023)

Surgical scissor tool joint angle estimation using ICP registration and tool CAD models.
